To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

photoplethysomographic (PPG) signals in the right index finger, recorded during occlusion of the left brachial artery, show correlated baseline fluctuations with the PPG signals in the left index finger.

the respiratory-induced changes in blood volume under a PPG probe, distal to the artery occluded by a blood pressure cuff, reflect sympathetic nervous system mediated changes in blood distribution from small arteries into veins.
the sympathetic nervous system can control blood volume in the fingers distal to an occluded brachial artery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new method to measure blood flow in the finger distally to an occluded artery, based on the respiratory-induced blood volume oscillation, measured by photopletismography.

the development of an optical method to measure blood volume in tissue, based on the photoplethysmo-graphic measurement of the cardiac-induced fluctuations in the light transmission, and the respiratory-induced changes in light transmission.
the use of the PPG signal for the assessment of the sympathetic nervous system activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the sympathetic nervous system controls blood flow in the capillary bed by changing the capillary blood volume.
photoplethysmgography (PPG), as a non-invasive method, is able to measure the blood volume changes in a distal finger in a subject with an occluded brachial artery.
the PPG signal is a combination of cardiac-induced and respiration-induced blood volume changes, which is mediated by the sympathetic and parasympathetic branches of the autonomic nervous system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the PPG baseline is a measure of the total blood volume in the finger and that the PPG amplitude is a measure of blood volume changes due to cardiac-induced blood volume changes.
the respiratory-induced changes in blood volume distal of occluded arteries are mediated by the autonomic nervous system.
the sympathetic nerve is activated by respiratory-induced changes in blood volume in small arteries and veins, and that this activation leads to a redistribution of blood volume in the tissue.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PPG can measure blood flow in a distal part of the body, even when the proximal part of the body is occluded.
the respiratory-induced changes in PPG baseline can be interpreted as a measure of blood flow in the tissue, and can be used to measure blood flow in tissues where the PPG signal is not detectable.
PPG can be used as a non-invasive method for studying the blood volume changes in distal tissues.
